dedupe_keys.name: peavy hall mass timber construction structural monitoring testbed

description: Peavy Hall at Oregon State University is a three-storey mass-timber research building with cross-laminated timber composite floors, a mass-plywood roof and post-tensioned timber shear walls. During the final ten months of construction, the university monitored wood moisture, temperature, humidity, wall movement and steel-rod tension to document how these systems behaved in situ. The Data in Brief article gives sensor placement and measurement procedures, and its public OSF project holds the readings, drawings and Python notebooks. The article is open under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; the OSF data licence itself is unknown. This is a real building testbed, not a general timber-building sample. Installation changes, construction-only coverage and varying sensor locations limit use as an operational performance benchmark. Its documented outcome is a reusable monitoring record and analysis route, not proof that a particular moisture or structural simulation has been validated. A reviewer-assessed use is testing model assumptions against measured construction responses. The related G2-0617 data deposit holds the sensor files; catalogue models model-wufi-hygrothermal and model-opensees are possible comparison tools, with no direct coupling claimed. No notebook or data payload was downloaded.

outcomes: The team instrumented the mass-timber building during its final ten construction months and published moisture, environmental and post-tensioned wall-response observations with sensor maps and analysis notebooks. The article documents the monitoring testbed; it does not report a validated long-term operational performance model.
